reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with the partition geometry. Tissue source site has the largest association magnitude (R-squared 0.349, q=0.0025) on the candidate-generation consensus geometry, with no detectable dispersion heterogeneity (PERMDISP p=0.286). On CT native geometry, CT phase (R-squared 0.154, q=0.0025) and manufacturer (R-squared 0.059, q=0.0067) are significant with accompanying dispersion differences (PERMDISP q=0.0285 and q=0.009 respectively), so their PERMANOVA signals may reflect both location and dispersion. Continuous CT acquisition factors are significant in their own BH family: slice thickness (R-squared 0.136, q=0.002), z-spacing (R-squared 0.142, q=0.002), pixel spacing (R-squared 0.019, q=0.035), and study year (R-squared 0.029, q=0.004). Reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and scanner model (q=0.054) are borderline and their PERMDISP is not estimable due to sparse levels. Interpreted jointly, measured site and acquisition factors remain plausible alternative explanations for an important part of the partition-wide signal; these are associations, not causal contributions, and no covariate adjustment or persistence-after-adjustment is supported.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, this analysis tests whether the current two-set partition as a whole is associated with measured technical, acquisition, or site factors. Several factors show statistically significant partition-wide association with membership: tissue source site (V=0.434, q=0.009), CT phase (V=0.316, q=0.028), CT scanner model (V=0.310, q=0.028), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared=0.066, q=0.026), and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared=0.048, q=0.028). These are associations, not causal contributions, and they indicate that measured site and acquisition factors remain plausible alternative explanations for part of the partition-wide signal. Manufacturer, reconstruction kernel, pixel spacing, and study year are nonsignificant, but nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding. This is a partition-wide technical concern that may motivate candidate-specific follow-up; it does not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and no covariate adjustment, causal control, or persistence-after-adjustment is supported by this analysis.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This partition-scope confounder screen complements the prior set-scope confounder reports, which described the same factor associations for K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 relative to the rest of the partition. Because the partition has only two sets, the partition-wide and set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal and not independent confirmation. The significant site and acquisition associations coexist with the prior biological-support reports (RNA and WXS phenotypes) and the weak, cross-modally mixed native-geometry boundary representation; these measured technical factors remain plausible alternative explanations for part of the observed structure and are not resolved by the molecular or geometric evidence.

Tissue source site has the largest association magnitude (R-squared 0.349, q=0.0025) on the candidate-generation consensus geometry, with no detectable dispersion heterogeneity (PERMDISP p=0.286). On CT native geometry, CT phase (R-squared 0.154, q=0.0025) and manufacturer (R-squared 0.059, q=0.0067) are significant with accompanying dispersion differences (PERMDISP q=0.0285 and q=0.009 respectively), so their PERMANOVA signals may reflect both location and dispersion.
